data.long_meaning: Reuelian is a Hebrew name meaning 'Friend of God'. It is derived from the Hebrew word 're' meaning 'friend' and 'el' meaning 'God'. In the Bible, there is a prophet named Reuel who gave Hagar the name Ishmael, meaning 'God hears'. This name signifies a strong connection with God and a faithful devotion to Him. The name Reuelian carries the meaning “Friend of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Reuelian usually hope their child will grow to embody friend of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The prophet Reuel or Reuelian, as he was also known, played a significant role in the history of the kingdom of Judah during the reign of King Hezekiah (715-687 BC). He was a descendant of the priestly line of Aaron and served as a spiritual leader and advisor to Hezekiah. Reuel's role was instrumental in the religious and political revival of Judah during this time, as he helped to lead the people back to the worship of Yahweh and to reject the idolatrous practices of other nations.
historical_references.context: Kingdom of Judah, religious and political revival under King Hezekiah

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Reuelian, or Reuel as he is also known, can be found in the Old Testament Book of Numbers (10:29-36). Here, he is mentioned as the name of a Midianite tribal leader who joined the Israelites during their exodus from Egypt and became a key ally to Moses. Reuel and his people provided the Israelites with much-needed military support during their battles against the Amalekites and other enemies in the wilderness.
historical_references.context: Israelites' exodus from Egypt and their battles against enemies in the wilderness
